ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular prism grid made up of many identical small cubes, with P and Q marked near two opposite vertices, indicating that a termite moves from P to Q along the space diagonal of the rectangular prism. The problem text gives that the dimensions of this rectangular prism are 3×4×5, with a total of 60 small cubes, and states that this diagonal does not pass through any edge of any small cube inside the rectangular prism. Reasoning: Regard the rectangular prism as being divided by three groups of internal grid planes. When moving along the space diagonal, each time it passes through an internal grid plane, it enters a new small cube from the current small cube. The numbers of internal grid planes in the three directions are respectively 3−1, 4−1, and 5−1. Since the problem guarantees that the diagonal does not pass through an edge of an internal small cube, it will not pass through two groups of internal planes at the same time; therefore each time it passes through a plane, it only adds 1 new small cube. The total number is the starting 1 small cube, plus all internal plane crossing counts: 1+(3−1)+(4−1)+(5−1)=1+2+3+4=10.

This diagonal does not intersect the edges of any small cube inside the cuboid. How many of the small cubes does it pass through on its journey?

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: it is a rectangular prism made of unit-cube grid layers, with P and Q marked at opposite vertices, so the termite path is the long space diagonal through the cuboid. From the text read the dimensions as 3 by 4 by 5 and use the statement that the diagonal does not intersect any internal small-cube edges. Model the cuboid as cut by internal grid planes perpendicular to the three directions. Along a generic space diagonal, each time the path crosses one internal grid plane it enters a new small cube. There are 3−1 internal planes in one direction, 4−1 in the second, and 5−1 in the third. Since the text guarantees no internal edge intersections, none of these plane crossings happen simultaneously. Therefore the number of cubes is the starting cube plus all plane crossings: 1+(3−1)+(4−1)+(5−1)=10.
